classification: INDEPENDENT CIVILIAN ECONOMIC RESEARCH — NO AUTHORIZATION, OFFERS, OR FUNDS
responsibilityStatement: Russia initiated the full-scale invasion of Ukraine; the OS does not equate Russian financing of aggression with Ukrainian self-defence or external assistance consistent with international law. Accountability, reparations, sovereignty and victim rights remain non-negotiable boundaries of this analytic framework.
rules: Humanitarian protection cannot depend on ceasefire bargains, sanctions relief or diplomatic concessions.
Pledged, appropriated, committed, disbursed and adjudicated compensation funds are different states. Do not add them together as available cash.
Sanctioned or restricted funds and parties require jurisdiction-specific legal review; no transfer routes or evasion tools.
Ukrainian government and affected communities control locally approved implementation; no coercive equal governance arrangement is assumed.
Reciprocal cooperation is contingent on competent authorization, explicit consent and independent verification.
The OS models public-interest options only; it never transfers money, makes solicitations, sends messages or predicts real actors’ preferences.

modes.label: Parallel civilian investment now
modes.description: Separate lawful actions may proceed independently without bilateral permission.

modes.label: Conditioned reciprocal confidence-building
modes.description: Requires a narrowly specified authorized agreement and independently reviewed compliance.

modes.label: Post-agreement cooperation only
modes.description: Cross-party projects wait for legal settlement, safe access and competent approval.

funderKinds.title: Russian state and state-linked war finance
funderKinds.constraint: Responsibility for aggression and the international claims/reparations framework are not exchangeable for co-investment or recognition.

funderKinds.title: Ukrainian government and defensive budget
funderKinds.constraint: Ukraine retains sovereignty and its right of self-defence; reconstruction and protection are not conditional on voluntary disarmament.

funderKinds.title: Ukraine-supporting states and public financing
funderKinds.constraint: Defense and civilian aid streams have distinct legal purposes; scenario cannot simply reassign appropriations.

funderKinds.title: Third-country buyers, intermediaries and financiers
funderKinds.constraint: Screen sanctions, beneficial ownership, export controls and conflict exposure before any engagement.

funderKinds.title: Defense manufacturers, banks and suppliers
funderKinds.constraint: Only voluntary, lawful civilian diversification with export control screening and worker protections.

funderKinds.title: Multilateral development banks and trust funds
funderKinds.constraint: Mandates, fiduciary obligations and government ownership constrain deployment.

funderKinds.title: Private capital, insurers and philanthropy
funderKinds.constraint: Avoid profit extraction, exploitative debt, greenwashing, unconsented risk or displacement.

funderKinds.title: Ukrainian communities, cooperatives and municipalities
funderKinds.constraint: Local consent, participation, national law, protection, and Ukrainian public-investment frameworks govern projects.

alternatives.title: Evidence-first reparations and environmental recovery
alternatives.mechanism: Maintain an auditable damage-claims-to-recovery sequence without treating victim compensation as negotiable sponsorship.
alternatives.proposedFunding: Potential adjudicated or otherwise legally established reparations; no principal release or confiscation is assumed.
steps: Document environmental and infrastructure damages through accepted claimant channels.
Identify which claims are registered, assessed, and adjudicated separately.
Propose protected disbursement controls for Ukrainian-led recovery only after valid legal authority.
alternatives.legalGate: Claims recording is not a payment award. Avoid claims of bilateral consent, waivers of rights or settlement immunity.
metrics: Eligible damage claims recorded by independent process (count, not paid claims)
Recovery projects with published independent audits (count)
Share of funded projects with community consultation (defined denominator)
alternatives.stopCondition: Freeze proposed disbursement if authority, claimant rights, legal attribution, or asset title are disputed.
alternatives.classification: UNVERIFIED INDEPENDENT POLICY OPTION — NOT APPROVED OR FUNDED

alternatives.title: Distinct defensive continuity and civilian recovery windows
alternatives.mechanism: Enable additional civilian reconstruction commitments without pressuring Ukraine to give up lawful defence or reclassifying restricted public budgets.
alternatives.proposedFunding: Existing authorized humanitarian, reconstruction, bilateral and multilateral appropriations, separately controlled.
steps: Map appropriations and legal restrictions for defense and civilian recovery separately.
Identify eligible recovery projects through Ukrainian-led priorities and existing funders.
Publish an additionality and impact matrix reviewed by Ukrainian agencies and donors.
alternatives.legalGate: No automatic reallocation of security assistance; only duly authorized financing decisions.
metrics: Civilian funding additionality versus a documented baseline
Approved repair projects completed after quality inspection
Number of civilian service users restored with defined methodology
alternatives.stopCondition: Halt if budget shifts weaken civilian protection or misstate donor pledges as payments.
alternatives.classification: UNVERIFIED INDEPENDENT POLICY OPTION — NOT APPROVED OR FUNDED

alternatives.title: Mutual civilian energy protection and green-grid repair
alternatives.mechanism: Pair independently verified non-attack commitments affecting civilian energy services with Ukrainian-led clean-grid restoration and microgrid resilience.
alternatives.proposedFunding: Authorized utility recovery grants, climate finance, and voluntary project financing; no quid pro quo for humanitarian rights.
steps: Seek separately authorized technical consultations on civilian services.
Define safe delayed reporting and independent incident-review thresholds.
Advance Ukrainian-owned recovery procurement independent of unverifiable promises.
alternatives.legalGate: Party consent and credible monitoring required for reciprocal obligations; no acceptance of attacks on civilians outside deal scope.
metrics: Verified civilian service interruption hours (baseline-normalized)
Independently assessed repairs reaching service
Share of new generation with resilience and environmental screening
alternatives.stopCondition: Pause joint components after material unreviewed compliance breaches or unsafe infrastructure disclosures.
alternatives.classification: UNVERIFIED INDEPENDENT POLICY OPTION — NOT APPROVED OR FUNDED

alternatives.title: Accredited mine action to regenerative food systems
alternatives.mechanism: Link nationally accredited mine-action land-release decisions to safe soil restoration, agroforestry, agricultural livelihoods and biodiversity recovery.
alternatives.proposedFunding: Authorized humanitarian mine-action grants, agriculture recovery investment and formally assessed outcome-financing pilots.
steps: Partner with accredited mine-action authorities for non-sensitive, aggregate release milestones.
Design locally requested food/soil/watershed restoration on formally released land.
Audit livelihood effects, land rights, contamination safeguards and maintenance funding.
alternatives.legalGate: AI screening never authorizes land release; avoid publishing suspected hazard locations.
metrics: Hectares formally released under national standards, aggregate
Area with independent contamination and soil baseline
Local producers with sustained market access after verified release
alternatives.stopCondition: Stop physical projects without signed land release, community consultation, soil safety or independent safety review.
alternatives.classification: UNVERIFIED INDEPENDENT POLICY OPTION — NOT APPROVED OR FUNDED

alternatives.title: Worker-safe industrial conversion and skills rebuilding
alternatives.mechanism: Assess voluntary repurposing of industrial skills toward civilian infrastructure, decontamination equipment, accessible housing and public transport where sanctions and export controls permit.
alternatives.proposedFunding: Voluntary company investment, approved workforce programs, and lawful post-agreement recovery contracts.
steps: Assess civilian skills and manufacturing capabilities at non-sensitive, non-operational level.
Require export-control and sanctions counsel before technology or funds move.
Offer protected worker training and independent product-impact audits.
alternatives.legalGate: No sanctions evasion, technology transfer prohibited by law, amnesty, or assumed Russian-party participation.
metrics: Number of workers voluntarily requalified and retained
Verified share of compliant civilian contracts
Independent quality and human rights audit completion
alternatives.stopCondition: Suspend on export-control violations, coercive recruitment, or diversion into prohibited military supply chains.
alternatives.classification: UNVERIFIED INDEPENDENT POLICY OPTION — NOT APPROVED OR FUNDED

alternatives.title: Voluntary regenerative R&D from defense-sector profits
alternatives.mechanism: Invite lawful defense-sector businesses and investors to additionally finance open civilian resilience research and repair training without compromising defensive security obligations.
alternatives.proposedFunding: Voluntary incremental funds separately reported from procurement or military aid.
steps: Disclose conflict-of-interest, beneficial-ownership and procurement links.
Fund open grants evaluated by civilian research and humanitarian institutions.
Audit additionality, avoid branding conflict profiteering as peace financing.
alternatives.legalGate: Donors gain no policy authority or immunity; export controls and anti-corruption checks govern.
metrics: Incremental independently audited civilian R&D grants
Deployments independently used by authorized civilians
Intellectual property licenses permitting nondiscriminatory access
alternatives.stopCondition: Terminate donor participation if contingent on favorable reporting, procurement preference or concealment.
alternatives.classification: UNVERIFIED INDEPENDENT POLICY OPTION — NOT APPROVED OR FUNDED

alternatives.title: Sanction-compliant energy revenue transparency
alternatives.mechanism: Explore independently verifiable reductions in conflict-financing opacity and fiscal incentives for lawful civilian recovery, without circumventing sanctions or changing responsibility.
alternatives.proposedFunding: No operational transfer: future legally approved funds or penalties subject to jurisdiction-specific review.
steps: Map public regulatory restrictions and legally observable revenue channels at aggregate level.
Seek licensed oversight of any proposed escrow or restricted-account arrangement.
Create a compliance-first humanitarian spillover assessment and independent reporting.
alternatives.legalGate: Never promise release of frozen principal or permitted transactions with sanctioned persons.
metrics: Independent sanctions compliance findings
Documented lawful origin of every committed funding stream
Civilian outcomes financed only after competent approvals
alternatives.stopCondition: Block any route involving sanctioned-party transfer without a valid license or authorizing instrument.
alternatives.classification: UNVERIFIED INDEPENDENT POLICY OPTION — NOT APPROVED OR FUNDED

alternatives.title: Circular rebuilding from screened non-hazardous debris
alternatives.mechanism: Compare reuse of professionally screened war debris with new extraction for reconstruction while protecting workers from explosive remnants, asbestos and industrial contamination.
alternatives.proposedFunding: Ukrainian project budgets, municipal recovery finance, external restoration grants, conditional private co-finance.
steps: Require contamination and explosive-ordnance safety assessments before handling.
Evaluate independent material testing and procurement alternatives.
Track material recovery, safe-worker conditions, and lifecycle impact.
alternatives.legalGate: No reuse before qualified hazard assessment, Ukrainian permitting, and waste-chain compliance.
metrics: Tonnes of certified reusable material (verified)
Life-cycle emissions against a defined alternative
Worker exposure incidents and material nonconformity
alternatives.stopCondition: Stop if hazardous material is mishandled, procurement is opaque, or traceability fails.
alternatives.classification: UNVERIFIED INDEPENDENT POLICY OPTION — NOT APPROVED OR FUNDED

alternatives.title: Municipal food and water sovereignty cooperatives
alternatives.mechanism: Build locally requested, contamination-safe water, heating, orchards and community-food programs on Ukrainian-approved sites with maintenance plans and public procurement.
alternatives.proposedFunding: Existing municipal and humanitarian grants and legally approved community investment.
steps: Confirm community-level priorities, land tenure and food safety requirements.
Use transparent Ukrainian public investment records for approved projects.
Contract verified local maintainers and independently measure service access.
alternatives.legalGate: Protected persons must not need to endorse any political settlement to receive food or water.
metrics: Households with sustainably restored safe water access
Growing seasons with safe locally harvested crops
Independent maintenance funding coverage and uptime
alternatives.stopCondition: Stop if source water/soils are unverified or residents lose rights or access.
alternatives.classification: UNVERIFIED INDEPENDENT POLICY OPTION — NOT APPROVED OR FUNDED

alternatives.title: Transboundary watershed and wetlands recovery
alternatives.mechanism: Design eventual consent-based ecological monitoring and restoration for damaged watersheds, wetlands and riverbanks without prejudging legal status or damaging critical civilian water supply.
alternatives.proposedFunding: Proposed remediation contributions and formally approved environmental reconstruction grants.
steps: Commission neutral baseline studies under Ukrainian law without sensitive geospatial release.
Compare ecological recovery to engineered reconstruction using independent impact assessment.
Draft a later-stage technical cooperation charter subject to sovereignty and security guarantees.
alternatives.legalGate: No shared site access or cross-border operations absent competent authorizations and safety conditions.
metrics: Water quality relative to independently recorded baseline
Wetland habitat area after independent assessment
Safe civilian water supply continuity
alternatives.stopCondition: Suspend if field work risks mine exposure, water access, or legitimizes unlawful territorial control.
alternatives.classification: UNVERIFIED INDEPENDENT POLICY OPTION — NOT APPROVED OR FUNDED

alternatives.title: Voluntary veteran and disability-inclusive livelihoods
alternatives.mechanism: Support voluntary, trauma-informed rehabilitation, accessible work, repair apprenticeships and community services for people harmed by conflict.
alternatives.proposedFunding: Approved health, workforce and social protection budgets, philanthropy and grants.
steps: Seek local health and disability organization review.
Create optional paid training leading to safe civilian jobs.
Measure retention and wellbeing without collecting identifiable medical records in the OS.
alternatives.legalGate: No forced demobilization, no employment conditioning of benefits, no exchange of patient or protected-person data.
metrics: Voluntary enrollment and six-month retention
Accessibility of jobs and training independently audited
Reported participant satisfaction aggregated with privacy safeguards
alternatives.stopCondition: Stop if privacy, informed consent, safety, or equitable access is compromised.
alternatives.classification: UNVERIFIED INDEPENDENT POLICY OPTION — NOT APPROVED OR FUNDED

alternatives.title: Claims-separated Ukrainian-led public investment pipeline
alternatives.mechanism: Use Ukrainian planning and procurement systems to match independently assessed recovery priorities with available lawful financing, without conflating recorded losses and payable claims.
alternatives.proposedFunding: Available legitimate grants, loans and insurance; separately track any future legally authorized compensation.
steps: Map Ukrainian-approved projects to documented baseline needs.
Categorize each financing source as pledged, committed, disbursed, or legally unresolved.
Create audit-friendly project review and public results records aligned with DREAM.
alternatives.legalGate: Registered damage claims are not an instantly spendable funding source; no automated financial transactions.
metrics: Funded approved projects with independently verifiable project identifier
Median procurement-to-service time with baseline
Share of published contracts passing conflict-of-interest checks
alternatives.stopCondition: Block if funding status is falsely presented, beneficiary consent absent, or ownership opaque.
alternatives.classification: UNVERIFIED INDEPENDENT POLICY OPTION — NOT APPROVED OR FUNDED

alternatives.title: Verification-gated civilian economic confidence-building
alternatives.mechanism: Evaluate incremental, reversible economic cooperation only when lawfully agreed restraint is independently assessed and protective obligations remain unconditional.
alternatives.proposedFunding: Legally permissible incremental civilian grants; sanctions relief or sovereign assets only after competent legal decisions, if ever.
steps: Define a narrow, civilian-protection outcome and independent evidence standard.
Draft distinct conditions for restraint compliance, humanitarian baseline access and project oversight.
Run independent civilian safety, legal and economic-externality review before any proposed benefit.
alternatives.legalGate: No financing architecture can grant immunity for aggression or compel Ukraine to waive rights or territorial claims.
metrics: Independent incidents reviewed under an authorized mandate
Authorized cooperation windows meeting transparency requirements
Beneficiary-reported service quality, independently sampled
alternatives.stopCondition: Suspend reciprocal economic components on serious verified violations; do not suspend legally owed humanitarian relief.
alternatives.classification: UNVERIFIED INDEPENDENT POLICY OPTION — NOT APPROVED OR FUNDED

alternatives.title: Independent civilian watchdogs for funding and recovery
alternatives.mechanism: Fund Ukrainian independent audit, investigative journalism, accessible grievance channels and local governance without giving donors veto control over findings.
alternatives.proposedFunding: Voluntary transparency grants, properly constituted donor audit budgets and lawful unrestricted philanthropy.
steps: Create conflict-of-interest and independent reviewer policies.
Fund public aggregate transparency reports alongside safe confidential whistleblowing channels.
Establish corrective action procedure independent of funders and contractors.
alternatives.legalGate: Protect anonymity and retaliation risk; avoid sharing protected-person information.
metrics: Published audit findings with remediation status
Percentage of projects with accessible grievance processes
Verified corrective actions completed with independent sign-off
alternatives.stopCondition: Halt if whistleblower security or reviewer independence is impaired.
alternatives.classification: UNVERIFIED INDEPENDENT POLICY OPTION — NOT APPROVED OR FUNDED
